body:
## Summary

Adds a complete historical analytics substrate to codevigil as a new `codevigil/analysis` package. The substrate enables opt-in persistence of session reports to disk, cohort aggregation over a closed set of dimensions, statistically-sound period comparison, and sample-size guards that prevent misleading results from thin data. Persistence is off by default; the schema is pinned at version 1 with a one-way migration scaffold in place for future evolution.

### Changes by area

**`codevigil/analysis/` (new package, stdlib-only)**
- `store.py` — `SessionStore` and `build_report`: XDG-aware storage path, atomic write via tmp→rename, schema_version 1, one-way migration scaffold
- `cohort.py` — `reduce_by` over a closed set of five group-by dimensions (`day`, `week`, `project`, `model`, `permission_mode`), `filter_by_period`
- `compare.py` — `compare_periods` with a hand-rolled regularised incomplete beta function implementing Welch's t-test from stdlib only
- `guards.py` — `guard_cell` (n < 5 → `CellTooSmall`), `guard_span` (minimum observation days), `cell_sentinel` helper

**`codevigil/config.py`**
- New `[storage]` section: `enable_persistence = False` (default off), `min_observation_days = 1` with range validation at startup

**`codevigil/aggregator.py`**
- Constructs a `SessionStore` when persistence is enabled; `_write_session_report` wired into `_evict_session`; write errors routed to the error channel, not silently swallowed

**`docs/design.md`**
- New "Historical Analytics Substrate" section: session-report schema pinned at schema_version 1, one-way migration policy, opt-in persistence model, closed group-by dimensions, sample-size guard contract, Welch's t-test formula with degrees-of-freedom calculation

**`docs/configuration.md`**
- New `[storage]` section: worked examples, activation log-line behavior, option descriptions

**`tests/analysis/`** (new, 151 tests across 5 files)
- `test_store.py`, `test_cohort.py`, `test_compare.py`, `test_guards.py` — unit tests
- `test_store_aggregator_integration.py` — round-trip integration test through the aggregator

**`tests/test_docs_sync.py`**
- Three new storage config sync checks ensuring `configuration.md` stays in sync with the `[storage]` config section

**`pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`**
- `pytest-cov` and `coverage` added as dev dependencies

---

## Exit criteria

- [x] `SessionStore` round-trip: write → read → deserialise produces identical report
- [x] `reduce_by` operates over the complete closed set of five dimensions (`day`, `week`, `project`, `model`, `permission_mode`)
- [x] `filter_by_period` correctly bounds cohort data to a date range
- [x] `compare_periods` computes Welch's t-test entirely from stdlib with correct degrees of freedom
- [x] `guard_cell` raises `CellTooSmall` for n < 5; `guard_span` enforces minimum observation days
- [x] `cell_sentinel` returns the correct sentinel value for guarded cells
- [x] Persistence is default-off (`enable_persistence = False`); no file I/O occurs when disabled
- [x] `SessionStore` uses an atomic tmp→rename write to prevent torn files
- [x] schema_version 1 is written to every report; one-way migration scaffold is in place
- [x] `_write_session_report` errors are routed to the aggregator error channel, not silently swallowed
- [x] `[storage]` config section documented with worked examples in `docs/configuration.md`
- [x] Session-report schema documented in `docs/design.md`
- [x] Doc-sync tests cover the three new storage config keys

---

## Test plan

- `uv run pytest` — 405 tests pass (151 new in `tests/analysis/`, 3 new in `tests/test_docs_sync.py`)
- `uv run ruff check .` — all checks passed
- `uv run ruff format --check .` — 102 files already formatted
- `uv run mypy --strict codevigil/ tests/analysis/` — success: no issues in 33 source files

Critical-path coverage (reducer and comparator are classified critical per test-standards):
- `codevigil/analysis/cohort.py` — 100% (74 stmts, 0 missed)
- `codevigil/analysis/compare.py` — 95% (129 stmts, 6 missed — all defensive Lentz continued-fraction underflow guards in the regularised incomplete beta implementation)
- `codevigil/analysis/guards.py` — 100% (36 stmts, 0 missed)
- `codevigil/analysis/store.py` — 100% (167 stmts, 0 missed)

---

## Deferred items

- `model` and `permission_mode` fields in the session report are wired as `None`. The schema and group-by dimensions are in place; populating these fields requires a future change to surface them from session JSONL system events.
- No renderer for `eviction_churn` or `cohort_size` metrics yet — that is future work.
- `pyproject.toml` version is unchanged at 0.1.1; a version bump can be done as a follow-on once the deferred fields are populated and the feature is considered externally complete.

author: rnegron
body:
## Problem

When `bin/start` launches phrocs, multiple Rust services (capture, feature-flags, property-defs-rs, etc.) start simultaneously. Each runs `cargo run --bin <service>` in the same `rust/` workspace. Cargo takes an exclusive file lock on `target/`, so only one compiles at a time -- the rest block with "Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache / build directory". With `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`, each service compiles single-threaded and serially, causing long startup times.

## Changes

Adds a `rust-prebuild` phrocs process panel that runs a single `cargo build --bin A --bin B ...` for exactly the Rust services in the resolved config. Cargo compiles shared deps once, parallelizes independent crates within one lock acquisition, and uses half the available cores. After the pre-build finishes, each service's `cargo run` is a ~0.1s no-op freshness check.

- `bin/mprocs.yaml`: New `rust-prebuild` process entry with `autostart: false`
- `common/hogli/devenv/generator.py`: Dynamic `_generate_rust_prebuild_config()` that scans resolved units for Rust services, maps service names to binary names (handling `capture-replay`/`capture-ai` -> `capture`), and generates the cargo build command

**Opt-in via `HOGLI_RUST_PREBUILD=1`** (in `.env` or per-invocation). Without it, the panel appears but doesn't auto-start. Default flip later is a one-line change.

## How did you test this code?

Agent-authored. Tested config generation programmatically:
- With `HOGLI_RUST_PREBUILD=1`: rust-prebuild auto-starts with correct `--bin` flags
- Without env var: rust-prebuild present but `autostart: false`
- With no Rust services resolved: rust-prebuild omitted entirely
- `capture-replay`/`capture-ai` correctly deduplicate to `--bin capture`
- All 440 existing hogli tests pass

Not tested manually with a live `bin/start` invocation.

## Publish to changelog?

No

## Docs update

No

## LLM context

Agent-authored PR. The approach was chosen to minimize changes (2 files, 61 lines) while integrating with the existing devenv generator pattern (same style as docker-compose profile handling, nodejs capability groups, etc.).

author: victorljn-earthranger
body:
## Summary
- **Compress chunks as \`.csv.gz\`** — reduces GCS storage and transfer size for each chunk uploaded to \`in_progress/\`
- **Separate archive deletion into \`action_cleanup_archive\` (daily at midnight)** — the old approach ran archive cleanup inside the 5-minute discovery loop, making N sequential GCS metadata calls (one per archived file) that were pushing the action past the 240s timeout
- **Parallelize metadata fetches and deletes in cleanup using \`asyncio.gather\`** — archive cleanup was iterating files one by one; with many archived files, sequential round trips would be slow; gather fires all calls concurrently so total time is ~1 round trip instead of N
- **Add \`sub_prefix\` support to \`list_files\`** — without it, cleanup had to list the entire bucket and filter in Python; now GCS does the filtering server-side, returning only \`archive/\` files
- **Include \`chain_id\` in all \`log_action_activity\` \`config_data\`** — previously chain ID was only in the log message text, making it hard to query; now queryable at \`jsonPayload.event.payload.config_data.chain_id\` in Cloud Logging
- **Rename chunks to \`{original_stem}_{chain_id}_{index}.csv.gz\`** — old names embedded the full original filename + a timestamp, producing very long names (e.g. \`DataForOrnitela_12345_20241215_234500_UTC_chunk_20260413_120000.csv.gz\`); new names are short, preserve the original file stem for traceability, and use a sequential index instead of a timestamp
- **Add \`chunk_index\` field to \`ProcessOrnitelaFileActionConfiguration\`** — needed to carry the current position in the chain so each triggered chunk knows what index to use for its name
- **Extract \`BucketPathMixin\`** — \`ProcessTelemetryDataActionConfiguration\` and \`ProcessOrnitelaFileActionConfiguration\` both had an identical \`bucket_path\` validator copy-pasted; extracted to a shared mixin
- **Add \`chain_config_data()\` method** — the inline \`{"chain_id": ...} if chain_id else {}\` dict was repeated 3 times in the handler; extracted to a method
- **Default \`chunk_size\` 4000→3000, \`batch_size\` 500→300** — tuned down to reduce memory pressure and give more headroom within the action timeout
- **Add \`ui:order\` to \`ProcessTelemetryDataActionConfiguration\` schema** — surfaces the most-used fields (\`bucket_path\`, \`process_most_recent_first\`, \`include_sensor_data\`) at the top of the portal config form
- **Improve error logging** — \`CancelledError\` from GCS has no message so \`str(e)\` returned blank; now falls back to \`type(e).__name__\` and GCS connection interruptions get an explicit \`"GCS connection interrupted"\` message instead of a blank error
- **Fix \`delete_after_archive_days\` default: 0 → 3** — default \`0\` made the condition \`days >= 0\` always true, deleting every archived file on the first cleanup run
- **Fix \`list_files\` prefix construction** — missing trailing \`/\` on \`sub_prefix\` caused GCS to match adjacent folders (e.g. \`archive2/\`); also moved \`list_objects\` inside the retry loop so transient GCS errors are retried
- **Fix stem extraction in \`_create_chunk\`** — \`split('.')[0]\` truncated at the first dot and embedded directory components in chunk names; replaced with \`os.path.basename\` + \`rsplit('.', 1)[0]\`
- **Add \`chain_id\` validator on \`ProcessOrnitelaFileActionConfiguration\`** — \`chain_id\` is optional and could be \`None\` when \`source_file\` is set, silently producing chunk names containing \`"None"\` and breaking traceability; validator auto-generates one as a fallback
- **Re-raise \`CancelledError\` in \`_process_csv_file\`** — converting it to \`OrnitelaFileProcessingError\` prevented the upstream \`except asyncio.CancelledError\` handler in \`action_process_ornitela_file\` from running
- **Increase \`MAX_ACTION_EXECUTION_TIME\` default: 240s → 480s** — 4 minutes was too tight for large files (4000 rows × 14 API calls); 8 minutes gives headroom, effective once \`PROCESS_PUBSUB_MESSAGES_IN_BACKGROUND=true\` is set
- **Update tests** — fixed broken fixtures and signatures from the refactor; added tests for gzip compression in \`_create_chunk\`, \`.gz\` decompression in \`_process_csv_file\`, and age-based deletion in \`action_cleanup_archive\`

## Test plan
- [ ] Trigger \`process_new_files\` — verify chunks named \`{stem}_{chain_id}_{index}.csv.gz\` appear in \`in_progress/\`
- [ ] Verify chunks are decompressed correctly and observations are sent
- [ ] Verify self-chaining: chunk 1 archives → chunk 2 triggered with incremented index
- [ ] Trigger \`cleanup_archive\` manually — verify old files deleted in parallel, only \`archive/\` prefix scanned
- [ ] Check Cloud Logging for \`jsonPayload.event.payload.config_data.chain_id\` on all activity events
- [ ] Verify GCS connection errors log \`"GCS connection interrupted"\` instead of blank message

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: ryebread1026
body:
Closes #1938, #1939, #1942, #1943, #1944

## Summary

The daemon's internal MCP HTTP server and Unix socket forwarding layer had multiple failure modes causing CI test timeouts, `ECONNREFUSED`, `Operation cancelled`, and silently lost responses. This PR fixes five distinct transport-layer issues that together caused frequent, hard-to-diagnose CI failures.

## Changes

### A. Align loopback host to IPv4 (`127.0.0.1`)

**Problem:** On Linux CI, `localhost` can resolve to `::1` (IPv6) for one component and `127.0.0.1` (IPv4) for another. Bun's `fetch` and Node's `http.Server.listen` disagree, causing `ECONNREFUSED` on the internal Unix-socket → Streamable HTTP MCP hop.

**Fix:** Default `this.host` to `"127.0.0.1"` instead of `"localhost"`. The `--host` CLI flag still overrides (e.g. `--host localhost` or `--host ::1` restores old behavior). Also threads `--host` through `DaemonManager` arg building and parsing so the override propagates to spawned daemon processes.

**Mechanism:** In `index.ts`, `daemonHost` changed from `string` (always `"localhost"`) to `string | undefined` (only set when `--host` is explicitly passed). The Daemon constructor only receives `host` in its options when the user passes `--host`, so the new `"127.0.0.1"` default in the constructor actually takes effect. Previously `index.ts` always passed `host: "localhost"`, which would have overridden any constructor default.

**Risk:** Low. Both values only accept loopback connections. The only breaking scenario would be an IPv6-only loopback host with no IPv4 — effectively impossible for Android emulator environments. macOS resolves `localhost` to `127.0.0.1` anyway so this is a no-op locally.

**Also in this change:** Clears the device-pool initialization timeout after the `Promise.race` completes (via `try/finally`). Previously, if device discovery finished before the timeout, the stale `setTimeout` callback would still fire and log a misleading "timed out" warning. The `clearTimeout` is a no-op if the timeout already fired, so there's no risk to the timeout-wins path.

**Files:** `src/daemon/daemon.ts`, `src/daemon/manager.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `docs/.../ci-integration.md` (expanded with this-repo emulator.wtf setup and consumer-app adaptation guide; no code changes)

---

### B. Serialize MCP socket forwards

**Problem:** Parallel JUnit test threads each have their own Unix socket connection, but the daemon shares a single Streamable HTTP client session to its own MCP HTTP server. Concurrent `callTool` calls on that one session corrupt the HTTP transport, producing `Operation cancelled` on in-flight `executePlan` and random transport errors.

**Fix:** Introduce `runExclusiveMcpForward` - a promise-chain serializer that ensures only one `callTool` is in flight at a time on the shared MCP client. Add `[McpForward]` debug logging (queue wait time, tool name, duration). Tag `executionTracker.cancelSessionExecutions` with `onclose` vs `onerror` reason strings for diagnosability.

**Why `describeUnknownError`:** The `StreamableHTTPServerTransport.onerror` callback receives `unknown`-typed errors that are often empty objects `{}` or non-`Error` values - useless when reading CI daemon logs. `describeUnknownError` handles all the weird cases (empty objects, `.cause` chains, non-Error throws) and produces a single readable log line. It feeds into both the `onerror` log message and the `cancelSessionExecutions` reason string so you can see *why* a session was torn down.

**`executionTracker.ts`:** Added an optional `reason` parameter (default `"unspecified"`) to `cancelSessionExecutions` and the internal `cancelExecutionsForKey`. The reason is included in the log line. Existing callers outside this PR are unaffected since the parameter has a default value.

**Risk:** The serialization queue means parallel JUnit threads' MCP calls are now sequential. If thread A runs a 5-minute `executePlan`, thread B's calls wait in the queue. However, the old concurrent behavior was broken - it corrupted the shared Streamable HTTP session - so this replaces "sometimes corrupts" with "correctly queued." Single-fork configurations (`maxParallelForks = 1`) see no overhead.

**Files:** `src/daemon/socketServer.ts`, `src/daemon/daemon.ts`, `src/server/executionTracker.ts`, `src/utils/describeUnknownError.ts` (new), `test/daemon/socketServerMcpForwardSerialization.test.ts` (new), `test/utils/describeUnknownError.test.ts` (new)

---

### C. Disable Streamable HTTP SSE auto-reconnect

**Problem:** The MCP SDK's Streamable HTTP client can auto-open a second standalone GET (SSE listener) after a disconnect. The server transport allows only one SSE stream per session - a second GET while the first is still mapped returns HTTP 409 and tears down the entire session, cancelling any in-flight tool calls.

**Fix:** Set `maxRetries: 0` on the loopback client's `StreamableHTTPReconnectionOptions`. Stale sessions are recovered via the existing "Session not found" retry in `runExclusiveMcpForward`.

**Risk:** None. The previous auto-reconnect behavior was actively harmful (caused 409 teardowns). Disabling it is strictly better; stale sessions already have a recovery path.

**Files:** `src/daemon/socketServer.ts`

---

### D. Floor `executePlan` MCP timeout to 10 minutes

**Problem:** The JUnit runner could pass a short `timeoutMs` (30s or 180s) which propagated to the inner Streamable HTTP `callTool`. When the timeout fired mid-plan, the SDK aborted the HTTP request, the server transport fired `onclose`, and `executionTracker` cancelled the execution — producing `Operation cancelled` even though the plan was progressing normally.

**Fix:** Enforce a 10-minute floor (`MIN_EXECUTE_PLAN_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000`) on both the JUnit side (`effectiveExecutePlanTimeoutMs()`) and the daemon socket server side (`resolveMcpRequestTimeoutMs()`). Extracted timeout logic into `src/daemon/mcpRequestTimeout.ts` with unit tests. `resolveMcpRequestTimeoutMs` also guards against non-finite inputs (`NaN`, `Infinity`, negative, zero) - falling back to the 30s default rather than propagating a broken timeout into `callTool`.

**Scope:** The floor applies **only to `executePlan`** - `resolveMcpRequestTimeoutMs` checks `request.method === "tools/call" && request.params?.name === "executePlan"` and only then applies `Math.max(base, 600_000)`. All other tools (`observe`, `tapOn`, `listTools`, etc.) keep whatever timeout the client sends, defaulting to 30s. The old code applied a flat 30s to everything including `executePlan`, which is what caused premature `Operation cancelled` on plans that were progressing normally.

**Kotlin side:** `AutoMobilePlanExecutionOptions.timeoutMs` default changed from `30_000L` to `600_000L`, and a new `effectiveExecutePlanTimeoutMs()` extension enforces the same floor. This means existing tests using default options will now wait up to 10 minutes instead of 30 seconds for `executePlan`. The 30s default was never viable for plan execution (plans typically run 1-10 minutes), so the old default always led to premature timeouts.

**Cross-language sync:** The `600_000` constant is defined in both TypeScript (`MIN_EXECUTE_PLAN_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS` in `src/daemon/mcpRequestTimeout.ts`) and Kotlin (`MIN_EXECUTE_PLAN_TIMEOUT_MS` in `AutoMobilePlanTypes.kt`). Both files carry `Keep in sync with ...` comments pointing to their counterpart to prevent drift.

**Files:** `src/daemon/socketServer.ts`, `src/daemon/mcpRequestTimeout.ts` (new), `test/daemon/mcpRequestTimeout.test.ts` (new), `android/.../AutoMobilePlanExecutor.kt`, `android/.../AutoMobilePlanTypes.kt`, `android/.../AutoMobileTestDemo.kt` (test), `android/.../SimpleIntegrationTest.kt` (test)

---

### E. Disable HTTP server timeouts + fix `id:unknown` error responses

**Problem 1 — HTTP timeout:** The daemon's loopback HTTP server is created with `node:http.createServer()` with no timeout configuration. Node

body:
## 1. Description (Problem)
When a workflow is started, the first (or intermediate) task may be assigned to the same user who starts the workflow. In such cases, the starter has already provided all data in the kickoff form, and the task assigned to them is redundant. Previously, there was no mechanism to auto-skip such tasks — the starter would receive the task in "My Tasks" and had to complete it manually.
**Where it manifested:** template editor → task settings (performers section); user's task list (My Tasks) after workflow launch.
## 2. Context
- Task #45866.
- Business demand: workflows frequently have the starter as the performer of the first step. Without auto-skip, they receive an unnecessary task, slowing down workflow progression.
- The change affects both backend (model, services, API) and frontend (template UI, types).
## 3. Solution
A `skip_for_starter` setting (bool, default=False) was added at the template task level. When a task is activated in a running workflow, the system checks: if the flag is enabled and the workflow starter is among the task's performers (directly or via group) — the task is automatically skipped, and the workflow proceeds to the next step. A checkbox was added in the frontend task performers section.
## 4. Implementation Details
### Backend (7 files + migration)
| Module | Change |
|--------|--------|
| `models/mixins.py` | New field `skip_for_starter` in `TaskMixin` |
| `services/workflow_action.py` | Skip logic in `start_task()` — checks flag and performer membership |
| `services/tasks/task.py` | Field propagation from template to task on creation |
| `services/tasks/task_version.py` | Field propagation on version update |
| `services/versioning/schemas.py` | Field in `TaskSchemaV1` |
| `serializers/templates/task.py` | Field in `fields` and `create_or_update_fields` |
| `migrations/0250_add_skip_for_starter.py` | DB migration for the new field |
### Frontend (11 files)
| Module | Change |
|--------|--------|
| `types/template.ts` | New field `skipForStarter` in `ITemplateTask` |
| `TaskPerformers.tsx` | Checkbox in UI |
| `TemplateEdit.tsx` | Default value propagation |
| `en_US.ts`, `ru_RU.ts` | Localization |
| 6 test files | Mock updates with new field |
### API
- **POST/PUT/PATCH `/templates`**: field `skip_for_starter` in template tasks (request body and response).
- **GET `/templates/{id}`**: field returned in each task.
## 5. What to Test
### 5.1 Preconditions
- Account with at least 2 users in the same team
- Access to the template editor
- Server running in dev environment
### 5.2 Positive Scenarios
1. **Skip first task (starter = performer)**
   - [ ] Create a template with 2+ tasks
   - [ ] Assign the current user as performer of the first task
   - [ ] Enable "Skip task if workflow starter is a performer" checkbox
   - [ ] Save template and run the workflow
   - [ ] **Expected:** first task is skipped, second task is active; first task does NOT appear in "My Tasks"
2. **Skip via group (starter is member of performer group)**
   - [ ] Create a template, assign a group (containing the starter) as performer
   - [ ] Enable the checkbox
   - [ ] Run the workflow
   - [ ] **Expected:** task is skipped
3. **Flag disabled — standard behavior**
   - [ ] Create a template, starter = performer, checkbox DISABLED
   - [ ] Run the workflow
   - [ ] **Expected:** task is active, appears in "My Tasks"
4. **Intermediate task**
   - [ ] Template with 3 tasks, flag enabled on task 2 (starter = performer of task 2)
   - [ ] Run the workflow, complete task 1
   - [ ] **Expected:** task 2 is skipped, task 3 is active
### 5.3 Negative Scenarios and Edge Cases
1. **Starter is NOT a performer** — flag enabled, but starter is not among performers → task executes normally
2. **Task with no performers** — flag enabled, but no performers at all → standard no-performers skip logic takes priority
3. **Returned task** — task with flag that was returned (`is_returned=True`) → skip still works
4. **Toggle and save** — enable → save → reload → verify state is persisted; same for disabling
### 5.4 Verification Points
- **UI:** checkbox is displayed in task settings, persists after page reload
- **My Tasks:** skipped task does NOT appear
- **Workflows:** workflow correctly proceeds to the next step
- **DB:** field `skip_for_starter` in `processes_tasktemplate` and `processes_task` tables
### 5.5 API Checks
**Outgoing requests (DevTools → Network):**
1. Open a template for editing
2. Enable the checkbox on any task
3. Click "Save"
4. In DevTools find the `PUT /templates/{id}` request
5. In payload → `tasks[N]` → verify field `skip_for_starter: true` is present
**Incoming responses:**
- `GET /templates/{id}` — each task in the response contains `skip_for_starter` (true/false)
### 5.6 What Was NOT Tested
- Mobile devices were not tested
- Load testing was not performed
- Production: verified only in dev environment
- Locales: text added in EN and RU, but locale switching was not separately tested
## 6. Affected Areas (Dependencies)
| Area | What to verify |
|------|----------------|
| Template editor | Checkbox appears, persists, toggle works |
| Workflow launch | Task skip works / doesn't work depending on the setting |
| Template versioning | Setting persists when template version is updated |
| Task cloning | Setting is copied when cloning a task |
| Existing tests | Mocks updated with the new field |
## 7. Refactoring
No refactoring was performed.
## 8. Commits
All changes on branch `backend/workflow/45866__skip_task_if_workflow_starter`:
- `feat(templates): add skip task if workflow starter is a performer`
## 9. Release Notes
Added a task setting "Skip for starter". When enabled, the task is automatically skipped if the workflow initiator is among its performers (directly or via group).

Adds unidirectional and unidirectional-unauthenticated cluster links.

unidirectional (authenticated) — cluster A consumes a token issued by B to create a one-way link. A pins B's certificate locally; B gets a cluster-link identity for A so it can authenticate inbound connections from A.

unidirectional-unauthenticated — cluster A fetches B's TLS certificate by address alone (TOFU with interactive fingerprint confirmation), pins it, and stores no identity on either side. B never learns about A.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Flips the `openclaw-config-sync` service from pulling config from GitHub to automatically **backing up local workspace changes to GitHub**.

The agent is the one updating these files, so syncing _from_ GitHub doesn't make sense as the primary mode. This change makes local → GitHub the default, with an optional two-way mode.

## What changed

### `openclaw.yml`

The sync sidecar now has two modes controlled by `OPENCLAW_SYNC_MODE`:

| Mode | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| `backup` (default) | Polls for local changes every `SYNC_INTERVAL` seconds. If changes are detected, commits and pushes to the remote branch. |
| `two-way` | Commits local changes, then pulls remote changes with `git pull --no-rebase -X ours` (merge strategy that **always prefers local** on conflicts), then pushes. |

**New environment variables:**

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `OPENCLAW_GIT_TOKEN` | GitHub PAT / fine-grained token with push access |
| `OPENCLAW_SYNC_MODE` | `backup` (default) or `two-way` |
| `OPENCLAW_GIT_USER_NAME` | Git author name (default: `openclaw-auto-backup`) |
| `OPENCLAW_GIT_USER_EMAIL` | Git author email (default: `openclaw@localhost`) |

### `README.md`

Updated the OpenClaw section to document the new sync behaviour and all environment variables.

## Notes on two-way sync

The `two-way` mode is intentionally conservative:
- Local changes always win on conflicts (`-X ours` merge strategy)
- If the pull fails entirely, it still attempts to push local changes
- No force pushes — if push fails (e.g. diverged history that can't be resolved), it retries next cycle

This avoids the main risks of bidirectional sync (data loss, infinite loops) while still letting you push edits via GitHub when needed.

author: gregmeyer
body:
## Summary

Second wave of the `/cso` remediation plan. Closes finding **#4 (chain trust propagation)** and adds the **MCP agent-scope opt-in** that was on the plan list. Also introduces `docs/SECURITY.md` — the public threat model strangers need before they `npm install`.

## What shipped

Four commits, squash-friendly:

| Commit | Theme |
|---|---|
| `4742022` | `mcp: true` YAML opt-in + MCP server filter + example/scaffold updates |
| `0c34acf` | Chain trust propagation + `UntrustedShellChainError` + wrap/block logic |
| `c4cd852` | `docs/SECURITY.md` + README threat-model banner + security-notes rewrite |
| `3218194` | Changeset (minor → 0.5.0) |

## Behavior changes (call out for users)

1. **MCP agents must opt in.** Only agents with `mcp: true` in their YAML are callable via `list-agents` / `run-agent`. Examples (`hello-shell`, `hello-claude`, `dad-joke`) ship with it enabled so the tutorial keeps working. New agents scaffolded by `sua init` default to `mcp: false` with a commented hint.
2. **Community upstream output is now treated as untrusted in chains.** Claude-code downstream prompts wrap the value in `BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED INPUT` delimiters and prepend a `[SECURITY NOTE]`; shell downstream is refused outright unless explicitly allow-listed via `executeChain({ allowUntrustedShell: Set })`.
3. **`executeChain` signature changed** — the fourth argument is now an options object. No internal callers exist so this is a clean API break for library consumers.

## What's defended

| Attack | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Compromised MCP client enumerates all agents | Full catalog returned | Only `mcp: true` agents visible |
| Community agent → local claude-code prompt injection | Concatenated raw into prompt | Wrapped in UNTRUSTED delimiters + SECURITY NOTE |
| Community agent → shell eval RCE via `$SUA_CHAIN_INPUT` | Silently worked | Blocked with `UntrustedShellChainError` unless allow-listed |
| Strangers evaluating sua's threat model | "read the code" | `docs/SECURITY.md` + README banner |

## What's deliberately NOT in this PR

The plan called out things that belong in v0.5.1 / v0.6.0, not here:
- Shell agent gate on community source by default (v0.5.1)
- Run-store `chmod 0600` + retention + known-prefix redaction (v0.5.1)
- Passphrase-based KEK for the secrets store (v0.6.0)
- Real shell sandbox via `nsjail` / `sandbox-exec` (long list, multi-day effort)

`docs/SECURITY.md` is explicit about each of these so nobody upgrades thinking they got fixes they didn't.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] `npm test` — 143 tests pass (was 129; +14 across `chain-executor`, `chain-resolver`, `tools`, `schema`)
- [ ] After merge + publish: `npx @some-useful-agents/cli@0.5.0 init && sua tutorial` still produces a dad joke
- [ ] `sua mcp start`, list tools via an MCP client, confirm only `mcp: true` agents appear
- [ ] Craft a community → local claude-code chain, verify the resolved prompt contains `BEGIN UNTRUSTED INPUT` and `[SECURITY NOTE]`
- [ ] Craft a community → local shell chain, verify `executeChain` throws `UntrustedShellChainError` without `allowUntrustedShell`
- [ ] Read `docs/SECURITY.md` on github.com, confirm all links render

## Design notes for reviewers

Two tradeoffs worth pushback on:

- **env-builder trust is NOT downgraded through the chain.** A local downstream keeps its full env allowlist even when pulling community output. Reasoning: strict `min(source)` would push users to silently relabel agents as `local` to bypass MINIMAL_ALLOWLIST. Template wrapping at the value level + the shell hard-block is where the real teeth sit. `docs/SECURITY.md` states this explicitly under the "Chain trust propagation" section.
- **`allowUntrustedShell` is per-agent, not global.** Required name match, so one stray invocation can't opt everything into the danger zone.

If `/codex review` or a second human review has a different take on either, happy to revise.

Fixes #353

## Problem
When running `flutterfire configure` twice and choosing to reuse the 
existing `firebase.json`, the command crashes with:

Exception: type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'Map<String, dynamic>' in type cast

This happens in `_writeDartConfigurationFile` in `reconfigure.dart` 
where `map[kConfigurations]` is cast directly without a null check. 
If the existing `firebase.json` was written by an older CLI version 
that didn't include the `configurations` key, the cast throws.

## Fix
Cast `map[kConfigurations]` as nullable `Map<String, dynamic>?` and 
return early if null, skipping that entry gracefully.

body:
## Summary

Add state sync support for `qmdb::keyless`, matching the existing sync implementations for `qmdb::immutable`, `qmdb::any`, and `qmdb::current`.

## Storage crate

**`sync::Database` impl** (`storage/src/qmdb/keyless/sync.rs`): A single generic impl on `Keyless<mmr::Family, E, V, C, H>` covers both fixed and variable keyless databases. `from_sync_result` initializes the Merkle structure from sync components, builds the authenticated journal, and verifies the last operation is a commit. Simpler than `immutable`'s impl because there is no key-value index to rebuild.

**`pinned_nodes_at`** (`storage/src/qmdb/keyless/mod.rs`): New method on `Keyless` that returns the Merkle nodes needed to reconstruct the tree from a pruning boundary. Required by the resolver. Follows the same pattern as `any::Db::pinned_nodes_at` and `immutable::Immutable::pinned_nodes_at`.

**`sync::Config`** (`storage/src/qmdb/sync/database.rs`): Impl for `keyless::Config<J>` so the sync engine can extract the journal config.

**`sync::Resolver`** (`storage/src/qmdb/sync/resolver.rs`): New `impl_resolver_keyless!` macro generating resolver impls for both fixed and variable keyless DB types (3 Arc/Lock wrapper variants each). Keyless needs its own macro because its type parameters differ from the keyed variants (no `K`/`T`).

**Tests**: 20 tests covering basic sync at various batch sizes, persistence after sync, target updates (increase, decrease, during sync, after completion), partial/exact match with existing data, resolver failure, and a fixed-variant test.

## Sync example

**`examples/sync/src/databases/keyless.rs`**: New module implementing the `Syncable` trait for keyless using `keyless::fixed` (since the example's `Value` type is fixed-size `sha256::Digest`). Includes `create_config`, deterministic test operation generation, and the `Syncable` impl.

**Server/client**: Added `run_keyless` functions and `--db keyless` CLI support in both binaries.

**`Syncable` trait bound**: Weakened `type Operation` bound from `Operation<Self::Family> + Encode + Sync + 'static` to `Encode + Sync + 'static`. The `Operation<F>` trait requires key-related methods (`key()`, `is_update()`, `is_delete()`, `has_floor()`) that don't apply to keyless operations and were never called through the `Syncable` interface.


Partially resolves #3538

## Summary
Fixed a bug where rematch state variables were not being properly reset when starting a new fight with the same opponent, causing stale state from the previous match to carry over.

## Key Changes
- Added explicit reset of `_rematchRound`, `_matchSpeedMultiplier`, and match series record in `startFight()` method
- These resets now occur before `startMatchmaking()` is called, ensuring a clean state for fresh fights

## Implementation Details
The issue occurred because `startMatchmaking()` only resets these variables when `_rematchOpponentUid` is null. However, after a completed fight with rematch enabled, `_rematchOpponentUid` remains set, causing the reset logic to be skipped on the next fight initialization. By explicitly resetting these values in `startFight()`, we ensure every new fight starts with a clean slate regardless of rematch state.

  - Uploads the PDF as a workflow artifact (90-day retention) downloadable from the Actions tab

```yaml
- name: Convert Markdown to PDF
  run: |
    pandoc PRESENTATION.md \
      --pdf-engine=xelatex \
      --variable geometry:margin=1in \
      --toc --toc-depth=2 \
      -o PRESENTATION.pdf
```

## Overview

This PR implements image upload and management functionality using Cloudinary.

It introduces photo storage support, database persistence, and deletion synchronization between Cloudinary and the application database.

## Backend Changes

- Added Cloudinary configuration to `appsettings.json`
- Installed Cloudinary .NET SDK
- Added `Photo` entity and database migrations
- Implemented `PhotoService` for uploading and deleting images via Cloudinary
- Updated delete logic to remove photos from both Cloudinary and the database
- Fixed photo deletion lookup to use `PhotoId` instead of `PublicId`
- Ensured users are retrieved with associated photos when required

## Technical Highlights

- External media storage integration using Cloudinary
- Database-backed photo metadata management
- Proper synchronization between external storage and local database
- Fix for incorrect identifier comparison preventing false `NotFound` responses
- Improved entity loading to correctly include related photo data

## Result

The system now supports:

- Uploading user photos to Cloudinary
- Storing photo metadata in the database
- Deleting photos from both Cloudinary and the database
- Correctly retrieving users with associated photos
- Reliable deletion logic using proper identifier matching

This establishes the foundation for user profile photo management.
